# Filters generated from (Area, half-life) targets drawn gaussian (sd 0.65, clip 1.35 half-widths) about the
# centre of each cell type's own cell of the largest type-separating grid.
# Source: Filters_ClandininData_Inverse.ipynb, section 4.
# Fit variant: UnconstrainedFit
# Modality: gaussian (sd 0.65, clip 1.35 half-widths) about the centre of the largest star-separating rectangle on a lattice, area 0.0274 sd^2 (modality 'inverse', section 4)
# Grid cell: 0.022829 x 0.009000 s, lattice offset (+0.021231, +0.002520), seed 1.
# Draw: normal about the cell centre, sd 0.65 of a half-width (the uniform's is 0.577),
# redrawn beyond 1.35 half-widths. 15% of the targets therefore sit just outside
# their own cell -- centre-weighted rather than a filled square, with the
# 11 types still separated.
#
# NOTE -- the spread here is set by TYPE IDENTIFIABILITY, not measured from the data.
# It is the largest variation that still keeps the 11 cell types in distinct grid
# cells; it is not an estimate of biological variability. This dataset cannot
# establish per-type variability -- measurement noise alone reproduces 44-104% of the
# observed per-cell scatter.
#
# Features are computed on t = arange(0.001, 5, 0.001), matching section 4 of
# FiltersClandinin_PCA_FeatureSpace.ipynb, not the recording grid.
# type   k   A_target  tau_target      A_fit    tau_fit        t1        t2      rho_
